name: hip fracture overview
title: Suspected hip fracture worked through the lecture's approach: is it a fracture, is the patient stable, why did they fall and why did the bone break, then surgery within 24 to 48 hours chosen by fracture type (femoral neck non-displaced or displaced, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric), and the after-surgery plan to prevent complications, falls and the next fracture

nodes.title: Suspected HIP FRACTURE (= a proximal femur fracture)
lines: risk = whatever raises the risk of FALLS + whatever raises the risk of OSTEOPOROSIS
high suspicion in an older person even if the pain or the trauma was minimal

nodes.title: 1 · Is this a hip fracture?
lines: sudden groin or lateral upper-thigh pain after a fall · worse moving and weight bearing
leg SHORTENED, EXTERNALLY ROTATED and ABDUCTED · cannot weight bear · painful log roll and straight leg raise

nodes.title: Work up in order
lines: 1 · X-ray: AP (front-to-back) pelvis + hip · negative but suspicion still high → CT
2 · STABLE? airway, breathing, circulation (young, high-energy) · pelvic fracture? · check distal pulses + nerves, especially the SCIATIC
3 · WHY did they fall? complete blood count (CBC), electrolytes, troponin · ECG (atrial fibrillation?) · chest X-ray (pneumonia?)
4 · WHY did the bone break? a pathologic fracture (bone tumour)? · a fragility fracture qualifies as OSTEOPOROSIS → start that workup

nodes.title: 5 · Plan: SURGERY within 24–48 hours for the VAST majority
lines: quicker return to weight bearing · fewer complications of lying still · the X-ray's fracture type picks the operation ↓

nodes.title: Femoral neck, DISPLACED
lines: the femoral head's blood supply is at stake

nodes.title: Options, not steps
lines: • maybe screws across the fracture (internal fixation)
• maybe NON-operative: only if VERY non-displaced in a poor surgical candidate

nodes.title: ARTHROPLASTY, hemi or total
lines: • surgery is REQUIRED to preserve the blood supply

panels.title: 6 · After surgery: prevent the harms of lying still
items: venous thromboembolism (VTE) is common → low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for 14–30 days
pneumonia: a common cause of death

panels.title: Regain function and stop the next one
items: falls: optimize illnesses, the home, occupational therapy and physiotherapy, gait aids
bones: vitamin D, calcium, secondary osteoporosis workup, antiresorptive
